title: Incidence of Metaphorical Virtual Classrooms and Interactive Learning Objects in the Interaction of Online Students: An Ecuadorian Case Study
reason: Re-extraction (inclusion not re-decided). Moodle metrics and grades are compared old-vs-new system at classroom level by Wilcoxon tests; no indicator is related to success or a construct. On full-text rules this would fail I1-I4 (NOREL/E4); flagged.

extraction.design: case study, before/after system comparison (Wilcoxon signed-rank), CFA on teacher questionnaire
extraction.n_quote: with a total of 1697 students ... for the first intervention period (semester 2023-A previous LMS) and 1859 students during ... the second intervention period (semester 2023-B new LMS).
extraction.population: online-programme students (law, basic education, international business, business administration): 1697 in 2023-A and 1859 in 2023-B; 224 teachers; 1 university
extraction.lms_indicators: per-classroom averages extracted from the Moodle database by a custom plugin: percentage of activities/resources completed (progress), interaction index (shallow neural network over Moodle metrics), average time spent in the classroom
extraction.outcome_or_construct: average final grade per classroom; teacher-perceived usability (questionnaire, CFA)
extraction.notes: n set to nr: participants are not a single sample. Students: 1697 (2023-A, old LMS) and 1859 (2023-B, new LMS), different cohorts; the analysis unit is the virtual classroom, 'the final sample consisted of the observations collected for 224 virtual classrooms.' Only medians and p-values, e.g. 'the average final grades for each subject of the students in each classroom went from a median of 7.55 to a median of 8.4, which represents a significant improvement with a p-value of 7.39 × 10−11'; interaction 44.92% -> 79.88%; time 8.39 h -> 18.01 h. Each LMS metric is an outcome of the system change, not a predictor of grades, so no indicator-outcome effect size exists. Table 2's 'interaction quality with virtual classroom objects' corresponds to the interaction index. The PDF text layer is partly doubled (track-changes overlay) in places.
